observations: Photo 0 shows a complete engine bay with a visible valve cover reading “DAF 24 VALVE” and “DAF” (also “HEPH AUTOS” watermark).
Photo 1 shows a large engine assembly with multiple hoses/intake/exhaust openings; engine appears removed from a vehicle and laid out.
Photo 2 shows the engine laid out with two valve covers/engine covers that both appear to say “DAF” and “24 VALVE”.

identity.model: 24 VALVE (as readable on the valve cover)

claims.claim: Clean and powerful Trailer Head Engine, in excellent condition and ready for work.
claims.evidence: Photos show an engine assembly, but do not prove cleanliness level, power/health, or “ready for work” (no running/video, no compression/test results).
No dyno/run test or diagnostic readings shown; only static photos.

risks.risk: Exact engine variant/spec (displacement, fuel type, model code) is not fully readable; pricing can swing a lot by exact DAF engine model.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine ID plate/serial/model code (or the full label) and the full engine name stamping, plus the gearbox/ECU part numbers if applicable.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used DAF trailer head/complete engine with unknown exact spec (worst-case match to the lowest comparable that still looks like a complete engine listing).

risks.risk: “Ready for work” may be false if there are hidden faults (leaks, missing parts, turbo/ECU issues, low compression). Photos can’t confirm.
risks.proof: Video of a start-up/run (cold start if possible) and a simple leak check; ideally compression test results.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven/unknown condition (worst-case: treat as needing inspection/possible repairs).

risks.risk: Photos may not show whether it is complete (some engines are missing alternator/starter/ancillaries or have damaged wiring/harness).
risks.proof: A photo checklist showing all major ancillaries included (starter, alternator, turbo, injectors, sensors, wiring harness, hoses) laid out and counted.
risks.if_unproven: Price as complete engine but with unknown completeness; if any key ancillaries are missing, value drops—so keep to the lower end until confirmed.

risks.risk: Potential mismatch with the seller’s “Trailer Head Engine” wording (could be from a different application/vehicle than expected).
risks.proof: Photo of the engine mounting/fitment markings and the vehicle it came out of (VIN/registration or chassis photo).
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming application may not match perfectly (worst-case: buyer may need extra parts/adapters).

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the engine ID plate/serial/model code (not just “DAF 24 VALVE”).
Send a short video of the engine starting and running (showing smoke level and stable idle).
Confirm what is included: turbo, starter, alternator, injectors, ECU/ECM, wiring harness, sensors—send photos of each included part.
Send the engine compression test (or at least a mechanic’s diagnostic report) and any recent service/repair receipts.
response.reason: The photos confirm it’s a DAF engine with “24 VALVE” text, but the exact engine model/spec and “ready for work” condition cannot be verified remotely from these images alone, so a safe worst-case price cannot be confidently matched to the comparables.
